declaration_stage: Before layout context rendering or layout reader predictions; primary native batch already running. This corpus agent has not inspected primary reader outputs or reference answers. Root reports it has not inspected primary answer contents at this declaration.
design: Restore source-native internal whitespace within exactly the already selected chunk word spans. No retrieval rerun, source-word addition, source-word removal, header injection or unit inference.

algorithm.word_boundaries: Python Unicode regex \S+ on each existing augmented source page
algorithm.slice: From first selected word start to last selected word end; all internal source-native spaces and newlines retained
invariants: Identical question, history, condition, selected chunk IDs, BM25 scores, query hashes, chunk order, headers and citation labels
Identical per-chunk whitespace token sequence and word count
Identical total evidence word count and <=960 evidence words
Original context exactly reconstructs from frozen normalized chunks
Every source page hash matches the original corpus manifest

reader_followup_boundary.native_tokens_include: System, question, headers and restored whitespace
reader_followup_boundary.overflow_policy: If any input exceeds limit, declare the whole proposed layout batch input-budget failure; no truncation, no subset launch, no repaired rerun under this protocol
reader_followup_boundary.primary_comparison: Same checkpoint, decoding, prompts and resource rules require separately frozen request and execution manifests before any layout native batch

limitations: This is a post-source-inspection development follow-up, not an independent held-out test.
Restoring whitespace does not recover missing headers, units, off-chunk facts or semantic retrieval failures.
PDF native text may itself have flattened or unusual equations and reading order; source-native whitespace is not certified visual equivalence.
No scientific gain is established by successful context rendering.
